questions: Which authoritative function owns discipline selection, cast eligibility, blood payment, cooldown and renewal?
How do targeted DisciplineTgt records and native sustained disciplines converge on player state?
Which functions consume every Active_Disciplines slot?
How are overt use, AI sound and zone or Masquerade policy enforced?
How do event-queue entries identify, renew, expire and remove discipline effects?

relationships.evidence: vdiscipline_int dispatches the selected player index and remembered tier
vdiscipline_last reuses the stored index and tier
a Discipline without Is_Instant enters the targeted-record manager
a native instant/passive power derives duration and schedules an owned event
accepted blood and learned-rank checks enter target-set commit
cast execution applies the resolved target payload after the source payload
vdiscipline_endall calls the shared teardown wrapper
the ClearActiveDisciplines entity input calls the same teardown wrapper
shared teardown removes owned timed Discipline events
shared teardown removes every tracked targeted Discipline effect

findings.fact: The compiled vampire sheet and save surface has thirteen learned Discipline slots and thirteen parallel active slots in Animalism-through-Thaumaturgy order; stats.txt's four later Numina records do not extend those arrays.
findings.evidence: The CBaseCombatCharacter datamap builder exposes learned base/current arrays and Active_Disciplines base at +0x1310/current at +0x1354 for exactly thirteen named slots.
findings.consequence: Selection, save identity and network/runtime storage use the thirteen-slot enum even though the authored file has seventeen entries.

findings.fact: vdiscipline_int and vdiscipline_last converge on one authoritative use routine with a separately remembered compiled index and tier.
findings.evidence: 0x100d8490 stores index at the player selection fields, resets tier on an index change, checks learned rank and calls 0x100d8830; 0x100d9750 calls 0x100d8830 with the same stored pair.
findings.consequence: Quickbar selection and cast confirmation must not implement separate power transactions.

findings.fact: The shared authority classifies Disciplines through the compiled Is_Instant flag: non-instant powers enter DisciplineTgt targeting, while instant/passive powers enter Active_Disciplines and timed-event logic.
findings.evidence: The stat parser stores Is_Instant as bit 0x2 at CVStatInfo+0x104; 0x100d8830 tests that bit before choosing 0x101e2da0 or the native active path. Current data makes Animalism, Dementation, Dominate and Thaumaturgy non-instant.
findings.consequence: Is_Instant is a native-path discriminator, not a literal promise that an effect has zero duration.

findings.fact: A targeted cast resolves its DisciplineTgt record, applies BloodCost modifiers, verifies blood and learned rank, builds legal targets, deducts blood once, increments the cast counter and applies source plus per-target payloads.
findings.evidence: TargetedDisciplineBegin 0x101e2da0 joins 0x101e1250, 0x101e0650 and stat-list reads; commit 0x101e2f50 performs the BloodPool mutation, source activation, cast-counter increment and per-target 0x101e3730 calls.
findings.consequence: Blood payment belongs after accepted target resolution and before per-target execution, not in the client or once per affected target.

findings.fact: DisciplineTgt is an ordered target/effect interpreter supporting shapes, filters, strata mappings, chance/default hit tables, projectiles and nested helper casts.
findings.evidence: 0x101e06a0 parses identity, level, BloodCost, SupernaturalLvl, overt/interruption/recovery flags, AoE, projectile and source effects; its callees parse ordered Affects_Table and HitTable structures.
findings.consequence: The remake needs a generic interpreter; five per-level hard-coded spell switches would lose boss, supernatural, template and helper behavior.

findings.fact: HitInfo independently composes damage or blood mutation, trait effects, AI state, player/NPC animation, flinch, knockback, particles, sounds and nested casting.
findings.evidence: HitInfoParse 0x101ddfb0 stores the channels and HitInfoExecute 0x101de660 invokes them independently; Cast 0x101e33c0 applies source and target halves.
findings.consequence: Gameplay duration and authority cannot be inferred from a cast animation or particle lifetime.

findings.fact: Native renewable powers derive duration from Active_Disciplines data, apply duration modifiers, enqueue one owned expiry event and record per-Discipline begin/end timers.
findings.evidence: 0x100d9220 reads CVStatInfo duration, folds trait modifier category Duration, inserts a shared-queue event and writes the player timer arrays; 0x100d8830 matches or renews existing events.
findings.consequence: Renewal must mutate the owned event and its timers rather than stacking unrelated modifiers.

findings.fact: vdiscipline_endall and ClearActiveDisciplines share gameplay teardown, removing both owned timed events and tracked targeted effects through their normal removal paths.
findings.evidence: 0x100db250 and 0x1033d8a0 call the same wrapper; it calls event removal 0x100cf420 and the 30-bit target-effect loop 0x101e3c80.
findings.consequence: Tutorial/script clearing must remove sheet, AI and combat effects, not only HUD or particles.

findings.fact: Nested Trigger_Casting records are internal spell graphs, not a player-facing Discipline combo system.
findings.evidence: The target interpreter invokes named zero-cost helper records during one accepted cast; no command authority branch, buffered input state or ordered cross-Discipline bonus was found.
findings.consequence: Do not add a combo buffer to reproduce Blood Strike return, Blood Theft or Blood Boil explosions.

findings.fact: Overt, AI-sound and interruption metadata are parsed and used as separate channels, but the final zone/witness/Masquerade policy is not closed.
findings.evidence: 0x101e06a0 stores Overt, TriggerAISound and three removal flags independently; the current files and help text describe safe-area risk, but no complete witness-to-Masquerade mutation caller is in the focused function set.
findings.consequence: The remake may reproduce classification and interruption now, but must not invent an immediate one-violation rule for every overt cast.
